name: How do I choose the right brightness (lumens) for hallway lighting?

mainEntity.name: How do I choose the right brightness (lumens) for hallway lighting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing the right brightness, measured in lumens, for your hallway depends on the size of the space and your desired light level. A general guideline for ambient hallway lighting is around 10-20 lumens per square foot. For example, a 50-square-foot hallway might need 500-1000 lumens total. Consider if the hallway has natural light, or if it serves as a primary pathway. Using dimmer switches allows flexibility to adjust the brightness. Our lighting experts can help calculate the optimal lumens for your specific hallway during a consultation.
acceptedAnswer.description: Aim for 10-20 lumens per square foot for general hallway lighting, adjusted for natural light and function. Dimmers provide flexibility, and our experts can advise.
